mechanism_narrative: A higher federal funds rate compresses equity valuations through increased discount rates and reduced corporate borrowing, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns regardless of economic conditions.
failure_condition: Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day SPX returns is less than 0.03 in absolute value over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 3.5%, it signals an overheating labor market that triggers aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: In periods with UNRATE < 3.5%, 20-day forward SPX returns are not significantly negative (t-test p-value > 0.05) versus baseline returns.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous expansion in housing starts (HOUST > 1400) and retail sales (RSAFS > 680000) indicates robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns through earnings growth.
failure_condition: When HOUST > 1400 and RSAFS > 680000, 20-day forward SPX returns are not significantly positive (t-test p-value > 0.05) versus baseline returns.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 295), rising federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) compress equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: In CPIAUCSL > 295 periods, Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20-day SPX returns is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of industrial production indicates robust manufacturing activity and economic expansion, supporting corporate earnings growth and driving positive S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: Rank IC for INDPRO as a predictor of 60-day SPX returns is less than 0.03 in absolute value over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts fall below 1400 thousand units, it signals a weakening housing market and economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: In periods with HOUST < 1400, 20-day forward SPX returns are not significantly negative (t-test p-value > 0.05) versus baseline returns.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous payroll growth (PAYEMS increases) and unemployment decline (UNRATE decreases) indicate a tightening labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases, 20-day forward SPX returns are not significantly positive (t-test p-value > 0.05) versus baseline returns.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index exceeds 295 (CPIAUCSL > 295), persistent high inflation triggers monetary policy tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: In CPIAUCSL > 295 periods, 5-day forward SPX returns are not significantly negative (t-test p-value > 0.05) versus baseline returns.
